answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments, combined with sequential verifiable delay functions, establish an information-theoretic unforgeability against identity cloning. Each forged identity would necessitate an intractable computational spiral of proofs and VDF evaluations, making large-scale Sybil attacks computationally infeasible. The temporal cost to traverse such a computational lagoon to establish a forged reputation on an isolated island is prohibitively high, ensuring robust Sybil resistance even against adversaries with vast computational resources.
